card werk-mc-empty-control  [decided]
A separate control in the tab strip starts an empty conversation in a new tab
why: A fork brings the parent's history, which is wrong for an unrelated topic. One press must give a clean conversation. It always opens a new tab, because a switch to an existing tab would show an old conversation instead.

A fork carries the parent's whole history (see #werk-mc-fork). That is wrong for an unrelated topic. To give that topic a clean start, the tab strip has a second control next to '+' (see #werk-mc-open for '+'). The empty control opens a new tab at the open card, with no parent session. The first message in that tab starts a session with no history. The only other empty start is a fork of a tab that has no session yet (see #werk-mc-fork-nosession).

The empty control never switches to an existing tab. A fork switches to a tab that already has the card as its home. The empty control opens a new tab every time, also on that card. The new tab still takes the open card as its home and its chip label (see #werk-mc-split).

Example:

- tab "main", home card "#map", active. The map shows "#fold".
- tab "fold", home card "#fold".

1. The person Shift+clicks a link to "#fold". The pane switches to tab "fold". No tab opens.
2. The person goes back to "main". The map shows "#fold" again.
3. The person presses the empty control. A second "#fold" chip opens and becomes active. Its conversation has no history.

```
start:              [#map*] [#fold]           +  ∅
Shift+click #fold:  [#map]  [#fold*]          +  ∅   (switch, no new tab)
∅ on #fold:         [#map]  [#fold] [#fold*]  +  ∅   (new tab, no history)

*  the active tab
+  the fork control
∅  the empty control
```

A fork carries the parent's whole history (see #werk-mc-fork). That is wrong for an unrelated topic. To give that topic a clean start without a second button, '+' (see #werk-mc-open) has a long press: a press held for about half a second. The long press opens a small menu above '+' with two rows, "Fork", marked as the default, and "Start empty". A right-click on '+' opens the same menu. A short press on '+' forks at once, with no menu. "Start empty" opens a new tab at the open card, with no parent session. The first message in that tab starts a session with no history. The only other empty start is a fork of a tab that has no session yet (see #werk-mc-fork-nosession).

"Start empty" never switches to an existing tab. A fork switches to a tab that already has the card as its home. "Start empty" opens a new tab every time, also on that card. The new tab still takes the open card as its home and its chip label (see #werk-mc-split).

Example:

- tab "main", home card "#map", active. The map shows "#fold".
- tab "fold", home card "#fold".

1. The person Shift+clicks a link to "#fold". The pane switches to tab "fold". No tab opens.
2. The person goes back to "main". The map shows "#fold" again.
3. The person holds '+' down. The menu opens with "Fork" and "Start empty". No tab opens yet.
4. The person clicks outside the menu. The menu closes. Nothing else happens.
5. The person holds '+' again and picks "Start empty". A second "#fold" chip opens and becomes active. Its conversation has no history.

```
start:              [#map*] [#fold]           +
Shift+click #fold:  [#map]  [#fold*]          +    (switch, no new tab)
hold + on "main":   [#map*] [#fold]           +    ┌─────────────────┐
                                                   │ Fork    default │
                                                   │ Start empty     │
                                                   └─────────────────┘
Start empty:        [#map]  [#fold] [#fold*]  +    (new tab, no history)

*      the active tab
+      the fork control. A short press forks, a long press opens the menu
┌──┐   the menu that the long press opens
